definitions.explanation: The outward behavior or demeanor that reveals or conceals one's true feelings or intentions.
A subtle sign or indication of something, especially an attitude or feeling that shows through one's behavior.

examples.japanese: {何|なに}{食|く}わぬ{素振|そぶ}りをする。
examples.english: To act as if nothing happened.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{知|し}っている{素振|そぶ}りを{見|み}せなかった。
examples.english: He didn't show any sign that he knew.

examples.japanese: {平気|へいき}な{素振|そぶ}りをしていたが、{実|じつ}は{傷|きず}ついていた。
examples.english: She was acting like she was fine, but she was actually hurt.

examples.japanese: {怒|おこ}っている{素振|そぶ}りがあった。
examples.english: There were signs that he was angry.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{帰|かえ}りたい{素振|そぶ}りを{見|み}せた。
examples.english: She showed signs of wanting to go home.

examples.japanese: {不満|ふまん}の{素振|そぶ}りも{見|み}せず、{黙々|もくもく}と{働|はたら}いた。
examples.english: Without showing the slightest sign of dissatisfaction, he worked silently.

notes:
READING NOTE:
{素振|そぶ}り (behavior/sign) vs. {素振|すぶ}り (practice swing in sports) — same kanji, different readings and meanings. This entry covers the そぶり reading.

KEY EXPRESSION:
{何|なに}{食|く}わぬ{素振|そぶ}り — "an innocent look," acting as if one knows nothing or has done nothing wrong. This is one of the most common uses.

PATTERNS:
- ～{素振|そぶ}りを{見|み}せる: to show signs of ~
- ～{素振|そぶ}りを{見|み}せない: to not show any sign of ~
- ～な{素振|そぶ}りをする: to act/behave as if ~

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {何|なに}{食|く}わぬ{素振|そぶ}り: innocent look
- {平気|へいき}な{素振|そぶ}り: composed behavior
- {不安|ふあん}な{素振|そぶ}り: anxious behavior
- {素振|そぶ}りも{見|み}せない: not show the slightest sign
